Failure Diagnosis for Coding Agents
Zheyuan 
Lin
zheyuanlin@smail.nju.edu.cn
State Key Laboratory for Novel Software Technology
Software Security and Compiler Technology Lab
 Nanjing University

Introduction
Coding Agent Failure Diagnosis
Observable execution traces
Agents repeatedly search, edit, and test.
Traces record actions, artifacts, and feedback.
A final outcome does not identify the decision to inspect.
Errors can precede both failure lock-in and visible symptoms.
Goal: rank candidate failure steps and expose the evidence behind each candidate.
Source: Zhao et al., Failure as a Process (2026), Fig. 3

Motivation
Failure Analysis of Coding Agent Execution Traces
A Real Directory-Handling Failure
Claude Code issue #1669 · user-reported tool sequence
Observed action
Reported output
Bash(cd …)
“no such file or directory”
Read(../../…)
“File does not exist”
Read(…)
“Read 40 lines”
Further relative-path reads
Repeated failures; user interrupts
What should we inspect?
The execution context used by each call.
The feedback available before the next action.
An earlier decision worth inspecting.
One successful read does not establish sustained recovery.
Source: bgrant0607, 25 Jul 2025. Condensed partial trace; the underlying cause is unverified.
